name: Laamtuk Thet
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Indiana University Chin Languages Research Project, publications page (chinlanguages.org/clrp-products), checked 2026-09-17.
sources.note: No Thor/Thawr publications listed (covers Hakha Lai, Lutuv, Zophei, Zotung, Paite, Maraic).

sources.citation: Mang Ṭial Khun. 2019. A Phonological and Lexical Comparison of Thor and Hakha. M.A. thesis (Linguistics), Payap University, Chiang Mai. 260 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: the word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the thesis. Ch. 3 'Phonology of Thor' gives syllable template CV1(V2)(C)T with tone obligatory on every syllable (sec. 3.2.1 p. 24), three contrastive tones /33, 31, 24/ plus allotones [22], [34] confined to polysyllables, and tone sandhi (sec. 3.3.8-3.3.9, pp. 56-63). No statement on word stress, accent or prominence.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Thor language' (downloaded via API 2026-09-17) — used only to locate Mang 2019 and Ni Cin 1998.
sources.note: Nothing; gives IPA t̪ʰɔːɹ³³ and cites Mang 2019.

sources.citation: VanBik, Kenneth. 2009. Proto-Kuki-Chin: A Reconstructed Ancestor of the Kuki-Chin Languages. STEDT Monograph 8. Berkeley: STEDT. (sec. 2.3.2, pp. 48-50 on Laamtuk Thet)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for Laamtuk Thet; only segmental innovations (PCC *s-, *tsh-, *th- > th-; *thl- > s-; *tl- > ts-; PKC *w- > ɣ-) and the note that it is spoken in Laamtuk and Ruavaan villages (citing Ni Cin 1998).

sources.citation: Khoi Lam Thang. 2001. A Phonological Reconstruction of Proto Chin. M.A. thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai.
